messages:
From: Tamara Liu <tamara@finflow.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finflow.com
Date: 2028-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production slowdown: elevated latency + 5xx, reserved throughput not meeting SLA

Jordan —

We started seeing a steady increase in tail latency and 5xx errors across our /generate endpoint starting ~07:50 PT. Our dashboards show a sustained drop in effective throughput against the reserved QPS on our Dedicated pool (approx -28% below committed during peak). This is impacting customer flows and our reconciliation jobs are timing out.

Attached is a short log snapshot and a quick chart extract from our dashboards. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal throttle or if our reservation is failing to allocate? We need an ETA for mitigation — customers are jittery.

Tamara

Date: 2028-05-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production slowdown: elevated latency + 5xx — FinFlow (urgent)

Folks — forwarding the customer alert (below). FinFlow is seeing sustained headroom loss on their Dedicated pool and reserved QPS not being met. Their ticket indicates ~28% throughput delta during peak. They are asking whether we're throttling, or if the reservation is under-allocating.

Quick background: FinFlow is on a monthly reserved contract (DF-5421) with a committed QPS profile aligned to business hours; historically stable. They use low-latency model variants and KV caching.

Immediate asks:
- Olga / David: can you triage allocation logs for the FinFlow pool (#finflow-pool-07) and confirm if autoscaler logic skipped a scale event? Check quantized model variants/eviction logs for KV cache pressure.
- Naomi / Marissa: prepare contingency messaging and (if needed) a temporary burst authorization and an Mx mutual action plan to send to the customer.
- Vivek: raising to you because the customer is requesting executive visibility and an authorization for temporary capacity if we need to exceed reserved for <24h.

I’ll run the 9:15 PT call and capture commitments.

— Jordan

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production slowdown: elevated latency + 5xx — FinFlow (urgent)

Jordan / team — short technical readout from initial triage:

Findings (first-pass):
- Allocation logs for pool finflow-pool-07 show a delayed scale event between 07:42–07:49 that coincides with the observed latency spike. The autoscaler computed a scale but the allocation request to the reserved orchestration plane timed out (intermittent control-plane RPC errors).
- During the timeout window, several pods returned 429/502 upstream as they exhausted local KV cache (high tail working set); we observed increased packing and tokenization latency for long prompts.
- No evidence of customer misconfiguration; the request profile is within agreed parameters.

Immediate mitigation we can action now (ETA in parentheses):
1) Temporary burst: approve a 3-hour burst authorization to allocate two extra GPUs to finflow-pool-07 (action: infra ops) — ETA 12m once authorized.
2) Route high-tail requests to a lightweight model variant that bypasses KV lookup (action: serving runtime) — ETA 27m with warmup. This reduces latency but may increase per-token cost; we will flag for the customer.
3) Force a cache warmup across pool and increase KV cache retention for FinFlow namespaces (action: runtime infra) — ETA 45m.
4) Open a control-plane RPC remediation ticket to investigate timeouts and add a continous-health check for allocation RPC (action: infra eng) — created JIRA INF-3245.

Attachments: I’ve attached the short allocation log extract and a quick SLO snapshot we pulled.

We recommend approving step 1 (burst) immediately so customer flows stabilize while we implement 2+3. If exec signoff is required for the authorization, Vivek — can you confirm?

— Olga Petrov
Director, Infra Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tamara Liu <tamara@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production slowdown: elevated latency + 5xx, reserved throughput not meeting SLA — actions and request for approval

Tamara — update and next steps. Thanks again for the quick report and for joining the 9:15 PT call. Summary of what we did and what we propose: 

What we did (completed):
- Enabled a temporary 3-hour burst to finflow-pool-07 (allocated +2 GPUs) to restore headroom.
- Routed high-tail requests to the lightweight model variant; runtime warmed and error rate fell to baseline within ~18 minutes.
- Forced a cache warmup and increased KV retention for FinFlow namespaces.
- Created a follow-up engineering ticket (INF-3245) to address allocation control-plane timeouts and to add RPC health checks.

What we recommend (for your approval):
- Mutual Action Plan: agree to a 3-hour, one-time burst at Redwood-listed burst rates while we complete a permanent remediation (attached MAP for signature).
- Proposed compensation: we will issue a 10% service credit for the impacted 6-hour window while we complete post-incident RCA.

Please reply with approval for the one-time burst authorization and the MAP so we can finalize via DocuSign. If you’d prefer not to accept burst rates, we can instead apply an immediate routing policy that downgrades to a slightly lower-fidelity variant for up to 24h (lower cost).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_finflow.xlsx (MAP), SLO extract. HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/record/DF-5421. JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3245

If acceptable, I’ll kick off DocuSign and have Marissa handle the credits.

— Jordan Blake
